The code gives score 9 -> 'C' (both terms are 1) and score 19 -> 'B' (only the second term is 1). Scores above 19 give 'A'. That matches the docstring at both thresholds. The review should check the inclusive boundaries and float scores near 9 and 19. The handoff refs A.txt and D.txt only repeat generic context and give no file-specific priority. A grep for the thresholds found no other grading logic. radon/cli/colors.py:48 and radon/cli/harvest.py:374 only map the returned rank to a color. raw.py and visitors.py have no part in this mapping, and complexity.py has a separate cyclomatic-complexity rank, so they get little time.
